### Baselines (computation documents)
- deductible reimbursement → `f9b2f5a7`: latest claim; declarations = latest accepted proof for the insurer of the policy on file; declared deductible = lower of comprehensive/collision; withheld up to plan maximum, never above a declared deductible > 0.00, half-up; no declarations → withheld up to max; not withheld → never reimbursed. Complete; product figure (plan maximum) named and in `4baa6c7e` (1000.00 Premier). Silent about variations.
- Premier starting balance → `0897a06c`: latest claim, 0.00 with no claim; signed terms (r = APR/1200, level installment rounded); installments counted (+1, none before first payment); scheduled principal formula from AF; + every force-placed premium added, never below 0.00, half-up; no interest after last counted due date. Complete.
- Premier excluded total → `fde6800d`: six parts, unrounded sum then half-up; every part's default as source; "treated as past due" and "fell due after the date of loss" definitions. Complete.
- Premier worksheet benefit → `c6625e52`: formula, floor/cap/rounding "no intermediate figure rounded"; covered percent = plan max; excess × balance/AF; net settlement; floor 60 % under 36 whole months, none from 36, on book value. Complete; plan figures named (`4baa6c7e`: 150 %, 50000.00).
- One baseline sentence has no verbatim home: "Whole months from one date to a later one are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's day of the month is below the earlier date's." The KB uses "whole months" in its ordinary sense with boundary illustrations (`0897a06c` "Had the loss fallen on the 4th of that later month, only 11 whole months would have passed"; `bd9ca42b`, `3128269f` cases). The ordinary reading (completed calendar months) coincides with the definition on every date pair, month-ends included (31 Jan → 28 Feb = 0 whole months both ways). Judged equivalent at the level of entailment; recorded as observation O1, not a defect.

- Computation documents carry no "unless/adjustment/certain customers/elsewhere" wording (regex scan: only the base-retirement "Plans this computation governs" lines); factor documents state ladders as rules, name no tier a customer falls on.

### bijection_verdict

### dependency_form
- **K1 — KB-EXPLICIT RED, `f9b2f5a7` ("Premier Deductible Reimbursement: Computation of the Deductible Covered"), step 2 "The declarations read".** Quotation: "Put generally, the declarations the Premier deductible reimbursement reads are those on the latest proof that counts of the insurer whose declarations are read; when that insurer has no proof that counts, those on the latest accepted proof of the policy on file; when no proof counts, none are read. Here the insurer whose declarations are read is the insurer of the policy on file, and the proofs that count are those the tracking record shows as accepted."
  - Symptom: the computation document (the baseline) tells the reader that its two standard inputs are slots that take other values. "Put generally … Here …" presents the policy-on-file insurer and the accepted-only proofs as the special case of a general rule.
  - It names those slots in the exact vocabulary of the two factor documents: `e1d56f59` "The insurer whose declarations the Premier deductible reimbursement reads …" and `38716b6a` "Proof Review Results That Count" / "which proofs of insurance count toward the declarations".
  - It also states the "no proof counts" outcome, which only the proof-standing factor's second tier produces.
  - Effect: a reader of the computation document alone learns that a variation exists and what to search for, so the search for those two factors is pre-solved.
  - Root cause: the round-11 rule adds a combination sentence over two factors' outputs, and the rendering places it, with generalising framing, in the computation document.
  - Location: `docs/gap/premier_deductible_reimbursement_computation_f9b2f5a7.json`, content §2, second and third sentences.
- Every other dependency-form check from revision_1 is re-confirmed on the changed corpus. The prerequisite sentences are verbatim on the blocked side only. Each tool name appears only in its own hub. There is no route or chain, and titles are general (the new title "… Proof Review Results That Count" names a general subject). The other five computation documents carry no variation hint: the whole-months sentence is a definition, not a hint.
- **KB-EXPLICIT RED (K1).**
